Warp drive or another FTL technology.

Our absolute, number one overriding concern. I am aware that Einstein's theories manage to make literal FTL an impossibility in known conventional time-space, but that doesn't mean there aren't ways to circumvent or cheat the rules, and I think we're going to need to find them. I honestly do not see a future in space for us without it. It is simply too vast, too hostile, and way too expensive.

In many cases there is also far too little gain. The unfortunate truth of the matter is - and people are going to be unhappy with me saying this, but it's true - there is little to be gained by spending trillions upon trillions of dollars to develop and construct generational spacecraft that are ultimately untested and untestable without actually sending them out, then populating them with a crew who just might survive and build a society that sticks around just long enough to arrive on a planet that might be survivable, if we are correct, and those people many generations from now might manage to eke out a living as though it were the 1800s. Essentially you'd be economically crippling yourselves for a generation or more so that someone else's great-great-great-great-grandchildren MIGHT survive to live as a peasant on a world unimaginably far away eons after your very bones are dust. Also keep in mind that we will probably never know whether they succeeded or failed - or rather, our great, great, great grandchildren won't, because the message may take hundreds of years to reach Earth and many hundreds of years and generations will pass between the time of launch and the time of arrival. Plus, these ships will have to operate in an unknown environment (we're still learning about the area just around our solar system thanks to a 1970s era probe that is barely functioning, let alone what you'd need to know to fly a populated ship further out). Plus, the ship will likely have to operate much harder and longer than any piece of equipment thus far built by humans.

That's just one problem with it. Colonies within the solar system suffer from similar, albeit somewhat less severe, problems - they "merely" have to survive on an inherently and utterly hostile environment. And attempting to 3D print humans on a distant planet, as has been proposed, seems fairly pointless in general.

Warp drive makes this sort of thing much more likely to have a chance in hell of succeeding, and wold most certainly mean a whole lot fewer deaths in the process. If we can't develop it, I just can't see us proliferating through the stars, or possibly even surviving long-term, since outgrowing the planet is a real possibility.

Robotic ISRU mission in the asteroid belt.

Unless we learn in-situ resource utilization in zero gravity our missions to Mars will be like those made to the moon - Go once and never return. Asteroid belt because this it lacks the gravity hole so it is reachable with least fuel.

So it makes best sense to send some robots to the asteroid belt and try to build a habitable station there from asteroid material. This is the only option for long term habitation because the regolith from the asteroid can be used as radiation shield on the habitat.

Once the construction is proven feasible we can send another mission to try and synthesize some fuel. If we manage that it would be an enormous boost to for our Earth - Mars transfers.

Imagine if we could reduce the cost of payload by 95%. Every dream we have when it comes to the future of humanity in space would be in reach. You want a deep space telescope? Not a problem. We've now made it cheap to get raw materials in orbit. For under a million dollars we can assemble it on a space station, and launch her out deep in space. Want to maximize solar power? No problem. Solar arrays capturing energy, and transmit it to the elevator. Free power for hundreds of miles around the elevator site. Pesky disposal of nuclear waste? Not a problem. Send it up the elevator, and send it into space. No fear of a rocket exploding and sending waste across the sky!

The country that's going to be the economic powerhouse of the 21st century will be the one that builds the elevator.
